title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Layer
summary: Coordinate specialised AI agents through governed, provider-neutral, evidence-producing tasks with explicit policies, permissions, budgets and approval gates.

intent.statement: Enable AGASTYA to coordinate narrow AI engineering agents safely while preserving specification authority, policy control, human approval and independent verification.
desired_outcomes: Every agent action is traceable to a project, approved specification or approved analysis request, policy decision and evidence record.
No agent receives unbounded tools, secrets, production access or autonomy.
Provider and model choices can change without changing core orchestration rules.

success_measures.name: Task provenance coverage
success_measures.target: 100% of dispatched tasks contain project, specification, policy and input-hash provenance
success_measures.measurement_method: Audit task records and reject dispatch records missing mandatory provenance.

success_measures.name: Unauthorised tool prevention
success_measures.measurement_method: Security tests and audit reconciliation of agent tasks and tool invocations.

provenance.rationale: Derived from AGASTYA Agent Control Plane direction.

problem.statement: AI engineering agents can generate useful work but become unsafe and untrustworthy when their tasks, permissions, tool actions, decisions and outputs are not governed by an approved engineering contract.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA has defined the specification and workspace foundations but no durable control-plane model for specialised agent registration, task execution, policy decisions or evidence.
impact: Unbounded automation could introduce untraceable engineering changes.
Provider-specific logic would weaken product durability.
Agent outputs could be mistaken for verified engineering facts.

business_context.business_value: A governed Agent Control Plane enables controlled AI throughput while protecting intent fidelity, security and enterprise trust.

stakeholders.name: Platform Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns orchestration runtime and provider integration

stakeholders.name: Engineering Governance
stakeholders.role: Owns approval, policy and audit posture

actors.name: Project Owner
goals: Approve high-risk agent actions and inspect evidence.

actors.name: Orchestration Service
goals: Validate, dispatch and track governed agent tasks.

actors.name: Scoped Agent Worker
goals: Execute leased task attempts with effective grants.

functional_requirements.title: Register versioned specialised agents
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall register versioned AgentDefinitions with capabilities, task contracts, permitted tools, risk, timeout, retry, budget and approval policy.

functional_requirements.title: Create governed orchestration plans
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall create a versioned orchestration plan only from an approved specification revision or an approved analysis request and shall snapshot policy and input versions.

functional_requirements.title: Evaluate task policy before dispatch
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall validate task input, agent eligibility, policy, budget, autonomy, tool permissions and approval requirements before dispatching a task.

functional_requirements.title: Execute durable asynchronous tasks
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall execute tasks through durable queue and worker mechanics with idempotency, lease recovery, timeout, retry, cancellation and visible state transitions.

provenance.rationale: Long-running work cannot block the main UI.

functional_requirements.title: Broker all agent tool invocations
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall execute every agent tool call through a registered Tool Broker that validates effective permission, schema, risk and approval requirements.

functional_requirements.title: Preserve agent evidence and truth state
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall persist task output, model/provider metadata, concise rationale, tool result references, cost, latency and verification truth state for each attempt.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The orchestration runtime shall persist task state before dispatch and recover leased work without losing evidence or duplicating non-idempotent actions.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Failure-injection tests terminate workers during task and tool execution, then assert recovery and idempotency outcomes.
non_functional_requirements.target: No lost durable task state or duplicate committed sensitive action in the resilience suite.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Agents shall never receive raw long-lived secrets or unscoped production permissions; tools shall receive only short-lived effective grants at execution boundaries.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Security tests inspect task context, broker calls and logs for secret absence and permission denial.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero raw credential exposures in agent input, output, events or logs.

business_rules.statement: A task must reference an approved specification revision unless its task type is explicitly authorised as a pre-specification analysis request.
exceptions: Read-only Analyse tasks may begin from an approved analysis request with project and risk context.

business_rules.statement: An agent may invoke only registered tools granted by the effective task permission profile; unregistered or ungranted invocations are denied before execution.
A high-risk, irreversible, production, security-policy, database-migration or protected-branch task must wait for an explicit approval gate before sensitive execution.

constraints.statement: The first implementation cohort is restricted to read-only Analyse and Validation agents at Autonomy Level 0 or 1.
constraints.rationale: Write, deployment and production capabilities require completed graph, verification, policy and tool-broker controls.

constraints.statement: Agent orchestration business logic must remain provider-neutral and execute external model/provider calls through registered adapters.
constraints.rationale: AGASTYA must retain product value independent of the dominant model provider.

dependencies.name: Durable task runtime
dependencies.risk: A durable queue, worker and event-stream architecture must be selected before implementation.

dependencies.name: Approved pilot provider adapter
dependencies.risk: Provider privacy, model capability and cost policy determine pilot adapter suitability.

bounded_contexts.name: Agent Control Plane
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own agent definitions, plans, tasks, policy decisions, effective grants and task evidence.

ubiquitous_language.definition: A versioned contract for one narrow agent capability and its controls.
A versioned DAG of governed agent tasks derived from an approved engineering context.
The least-privilege tool, data and environment permission set evaluated for one task.
A policy-defined human decision required before a sensitive action may execute.

workflows.name: Execute a read-only governed analysis task
workflows.trigger: An authorised user requests analysis against approved engineering context.

steps.action: Validates task input, agent eligibility, policy, budget and effective grant.
steps.result: Task is blocked, waits for approval or is queued with a policy snapshot.

steps.action: Leases and executes the task through a provider adapter using only registered read tools.
steps.result: Output, tool evidence and concise rationale are persisted.

steps.action: Records task truth state and required next verification.
steps.result: Output is clearly marked proposal, partial, blocked, failed or verified according to evidence.

outcomes: A governed agent result is traceable to context and policy.
No authority is claimed without verification.
workflows.error_handling: Provider, worker, tool and policy failures produce durable visible task states and evidence.

states.name: WAITING_APPROVAL
states.description: Sensitive action paused for human decision.

security_requirements.statement: Every task and tool invocation shall be project-scoped, authorised and audited; agents shall never receive raw long-lived secrets.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security tests inspect effective grants and records for permission denial, secret redaction and cross-project isolation.

observability_requirements.statement: Every task state transition, provider attempt, tool invocation, policy decision and approval gate shall emit a structured correlated event.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests reconstruct a task lifecycle from durable events and audit records.

acceptance_criteria.title: Read-only task receives governed provenance
acceptance_criteria.given: A registered read-only agent and approved engineering context.
acceptance_criteria.when: An authorised user submits a valid analysis task.
acceptance_criteria.then: The task is queued with immutable input hash, specification/project provenance, policy snapshot and least-privilege grant.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unpermitted tool call is stopped by broker
acceptance_criteria.given: A task whose effective grant excludes a requested tool.
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent attempts the tool invocation.
acceptance_criteria.then: The broker denies before execution and records a policy decision and audit evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Sensitive task waits for approval
acceptance_criteria.given: A task requiring a protected write, migration, production or high-risk action.
acceptance_criteria.when: The plan reaches the sensitive action.
acceptance_criteria.then: Task state becomes WAITING_APPROVAL and no action executes before an authorised approval decision.

acceptance_criteria.title: Task recovers from worker failure
acceptance_criteria.given: A leased task with idempotent tool invocation state.
acceptance_criteria.when: The worker dies before completion and lease expires.
acceptance_criteria.then: Recovery follows retry policy, preserves evidence and does not duplicate committed tool action.

acceptance_criteria.title: Agent output states its verification truth
acceptance_criteria.given: An agent completes a proposal while independent verification is pending.
acceptance_criteria.when: A user reads the task result.
acceptance_criteria.then: Output is marked proposal or unverified rather than verified and includes required next evidence.

test_requirements.scope: Registry, plan compilation and task provenance generation for read-only pilot tasks.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Task record with valid contracts, input hash, policy snapshot and effective grant.

test_requirements.scope: Tool broker denial and human approval gate enforcement.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: No tool execution before denied/approval-required decisions; auditable policy records.

test_requirements.scope: Worker crash, lease recovery, retry and task/tool idempotency.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Failure-injection report with durable state and no duplicated committed action.

test_requirements.scope: Evidence, provider/model metadata and truth-state presentation.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Completed task fixtures demonstrate proposal/unverified/verified state distinctions.

risks.title: Agent autonomy exceeds verification capability
risks.description: Agent actions could outrun the ability to prove conformance and safety.
risks.mitigation: Restrict the first cohort to Level 0/1 read-only tasks and require independent verification before verified status.

risks.title: Provider adapter creates hidden lock-in or data leakage
risks.description: A provider-specific integration may violate privacy policy or embed core workflow assumptions.
risks.mitigation: Use provider-neutral invocation contracts, adapter metadata and explicit privacy/model routing policies.

open_questions.question: Which first provider adapter and model privacy profile will be approved for the read-only pilot?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Provider Adapter implementation and pilot data boundaries cannot be selected.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a design-phase risk. Provider and privacy selection is a mandatory gate before any external model invocation.

open_questions.question: Which durable queue, worker and event-stream deployment architecture satisfies the required retry, security and operational SLOs?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: P2 runtime implementation cannot proceed safely.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a design-phase risk. Queue, worker and event-stream architecture is a mandatory ADR gate before runtime implementation.

architecture_decisions.title: Use a durable task state machine and scoped worker model
architecture_decisions.context: Agent calls are long-running and failure-prone; request-thread execution cannot preserve state or support secure policy gates.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use a durable task store, queue, lease-based workers, idempotency keys and event stream for all agent tasks.

alternatives.name: Synchronous API execution
alternatives.summary: Execute provider calls on the request thread.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Blocks UI, loses resilient state and cannot safely coordinate long-running work.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Durable task execution is required for evidence, retries, approvals and observable state.
consequences: A queue/worker deployment decision is required.
Task and tool idempotency contracts are mandatory.

provenance.rationale: Agent orchestration must execute from governed engineering intent.

coverage_summary.method: Initial draft traceability mapping; code and runtime coverage are not yet applicable.

change_history.reason: Create the governed P2 control-plane contract before selecting providers, tools or runtime architecture.

change_history.summary: Multi-Agent Orchestration Layer approved for controlled pilot design.
change_history.reason: The Project Sponsor approved the governed Level 0/1 orchestration contract.
